A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decoding-calibration research, renamed from PC-Sampler to UNCODE. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, decoding-trajectory interventions, efficiency experiments, and case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark results and reports additional suppression interventions, decoding-dynamics analyses, and calibration-corpus experiments.

M1.justification: The positional weighting and frequency calibration remain. However, Section 4.2 changes clipping: v1 clips confidence multiplied by negative log frequency, while v3 clips negative log frequency before multiplication. V3 also introduces entropy-based automatic λ selection in Appendix A.10 and a calibrated-score adaptation for Fast-dLLM.

E1.justification: The seven downstream benchmarks and their tasks remain unchanged. Auxiliary calibration-data coverage expands to C4 and SlimPajama, with a BookCorpusOpen/OpenR1-Math mixture retained as a comparison in v3 Appendix A.11.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator set is retained. Strict left-to-right decoding disappears from the trajectory-performance comparisons. V3 adds Fast-dLLM to the efficiency-integration comparison and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct as the trivial-token-rate reference in Figure 3.

E3.justification: Calibration changes from v1's mixture of book, mathematical, and evaluation datasets to a 16 GB C4 subset. V3 revises the trivial-token definition, explicitly excluding end-of-text padding. It also introduces probabilistic token rejection, anchor-insertion controls, and entropy-based calibration-subset protocols. Component ablations now report seven-task averages on two backbones instead of two task-specific results on LLaDA.

E4.justification: V3 adds trivial-token suppression experiments, answer-entropy dynamics, entropy–performance correlations, calibration-source and size ablations, and another GSM8K case study. The boundary-masking intervention is replaced by anchor insertion, and component ablations are substantially revised. The existing λ/α sensitivity study is retained and moved to Appendix A.9.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix A.10 newly estimates Pearson correlations between predictive entropy and task performance across λ settings. Both versions retain seed 42 and deterministic-temperature settings; neither introduces repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises baseline scores: LLaDA confidence accuracy on GSM8K changes from 6.8 to 59.1, and entropy accuracy from 2.2 to 60.9. The proposed method's LLaDA average changes from 42.3 to 42.7; its LLaDA-1.5 and Dream averages remain 44.7 and 40.1. Numerous diagnostic and integration results are added. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix A.10 introduces formal sequence-level and dataset-level predictive-entropy definitions and the entropy-minimization objective for selecting λ, in Equations 13–16. The earlier version lacks this mathematical formulation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The headline average improvement decreases from over 10% to over 7%, and the claim that LLaDA-1.5 surpasses Qwen-2.5 becomes comparable performance. The central contributions—diagnosing decoding biases and combining positional and frequency calibration—remain despite the new title and terminology.

C2.justification: V3 expands the boundary-bias explanation around training templates and local positional effects, and explains how early punctuation creates restrictive structural commitments. It adds interpretations of entropy reduction and calibration-corpus saturation. A new Limitations section discusses label-dependent manual λ tuning and additional inference overhead.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies test-set counts, exact response lengths, four A100 GPUs, and integration details including the calibrated Fast-dLLM threshold and prefix caching. Seed, temperature, prompts, and evaluation frameworks were already documented. The advertised code location changes, while v1's explicit Fast-dLLM block-count exceptions are no longer stated.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused from broad diffusion history, planning, and remasking toward uncertainty-driven decoding and its systematic biases. V3 adds research on learned decoding order, lookahead decoding, adaptive sampling, and positional bias, including Garg, Lee, Horvitz, and Wu, while removing much of the earlier image/audio diffusion background.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, introduction, related work, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten around decoding biases. Experimental sections are reorganized, hyperparameter discussion moves to the appendix, and limitations and several appendix subsections are added.

P2.justification: V3 adds an opening illustration and multiple diagnostic figures and tables, redraws trajectory and ablation displays, and replaces the efficiency plot with Table 2. Hyperparameter plots move to the appendix, existing case-study tables become redesigned figures, and another case is added. The document template and visual layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V3 provides more direct evidence for the bias explanation through suppression and anchor interventions, improves calibration documentation and sensitivity analysis, and states clearer limitations and more restrained performance claims. These strengthen the paper. However, large baseline revisions remain unexplained, and numerical inconsistencies persist: Qwen's Countdown score is 7.7 in Table 1 but 0.0 in Table 5. These reporting problems limit the overall improvement.
